entries.title: RULES.md is the sole rulebook; read README.md then RULES.md before any work
entries.text: Read root README.md and RULES.md completely at session start and after compaction. RULES.md is the only authority for safety, production-data compatibility (rule 11: expand-first migrations, no destructive changes without a separate maintainer decision), no new source comments (rule 9), critical-only tests (rule 10), Git identity and authorization (rule 14), and verification. Never deploy, touch the VPS, move real money, or send real customer mail. This tally entry points there and does not restate or override it.
entries.retiredWhy: replaced by rule-16

entries.title: Maintainer decision 2026-11-13: AutoPay and normal online payments stay disabled until the maintainer enables them
entries.text: Decision (maintainer, 2026-11-13, in chat): AutoPay and normal (one-time gateway checkout) payments are turned off for the time being and remain disabled unless the maintainer decides to activate them. Agents never enable them, never change payment env keys, and never treat a fix as permission to re-enable. Implications for planning: admin offline recording (recordContribution, incl. the new monthly-investment category) is the primary way investments enter the ledger; the AutoPay next_due_date bug (finding-6) becomes a must-fix-before-re-enable item rather than urgent; DD point 6 SIP months-paid must count offline-recorded monthly investments to be meaningful; question row 7 (AutoPay on web) is deferred. Known switches (STATIC): AutoPay via PHONEPE_AUTOPAY_ENABLED / PHONEPE_AUTOPAY_COLLECTION_ENABLED (default false, environment.ts:101-102); one-time checkout has no dedicated flag, only removing the relay (PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL/SECRET) which makes POST pay return a generic DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE (clientOrderRoutes.ts:154-156). To be recorded in the next plan's decision record.
entries.retiredWhy: replaced by rule-14

entries.title: Decision 2026-11-13 (Q1): keep client and investment records on dev and prod; prod data reform via tested one-time step
entries.text: Maintainer answer to question row 1. Dev server may be cleaned, but on BOTH dev and production client records and investment records stay intact. Production manages real clients. Approach: save a copy of the required information from the production database, then in the next deployed update run a one-time migration/copy step that reforms the database with proper client data without losing any of it; rehearse that step on the dev server first. Constraints from RULES: the maintainer performs every production export and deploy (rule 2/3); a reform that rewrites, backfills or removes rows is a destructive change under rule 11 needing the recorded pre-flight check, refusal-on-loss, populated-upgrade test and rollback-boundary registration; ledger/order/payment/audit/consent/application/delivery rows are never deleted or rewritten, corrections are new rows. Open: what exactly is wrong in the current data (follow-up question), and how production PII copied to dev is protected.
entries.retiredWhy: Question answers are decisions, not rules (maintainer 2026-11-14). Recorded as decision DEC-1, group admin-improvements.

entries.title: Decision 2026-11-13 (Q2): clients see each admin recording as a receipt labelled by its category
entries.text: Maintainer answer to question row 2. When the admin records an investment (earlier investment, correction, monthly investment, and further categories), the client sees it like a receipt, labelled with the category the admin chose. Implementation must stay additive so released APKs keep working (RULES rule 11): prefer a new client endpoint/screen and category-aware notification over changing existing response shapes or enums, unless the design check shows the change is tolerated. The notification text must follow the category instead of the fixed 'before you joined the app' copy.
entries.retiredWhy: Question answers are decisions, not rules (maintainer 2026-11-14). Recorded as decision DEC-2, group admin-improvements.

entries.title: Decision 2026-11-13 (Q3): no automatic maturity; admin maturity dates, dashboard, prompt on every admin open
entries.text: Maintainer answer to question row 3. No automatic maturity. Admin enters a maturity date. A specialised maturity management dashboard lists them. When a maturity date nears, the admin is notified every time the admin app is opened and asked to resolve it with one of: (1) return all the money to the client; (2) record it as a one-time investment that starts from the maturity date and from then start a new SIP; (3) reinvest the money as a SIP. Every recording counts; the admin manages and updates them. No payout or ledger change ever happens without the admin's explicit resolution. Real bank transfer stays outside the app (existing withdrawal payout flow).
entries.retiredWhy: Question answers are decisions, not rules (maintainer 2026-11-14). Recorded as decisions DEC-3 and DEC-15, group admin-improvements.

entries.title: Decisions 2026-11-13 (Q4-Q8): nominee+relation, onboarding only, reviews, AutoPay off, growth records notify clients
entries.text: Maintainer answers. Q4: nominee name with relation to the account holder. Q5: public signups are not in use; only admin onboarding of clients is used, so DD point 3 (signup redirect) is not pursued; audit the onboarding process for bugs. Q6: signup application reviews stay as they are; admin onboarding works well today and does not go through review (answer did not address DD point 1 client app reviews/comments; follow-up question). Q7: AutoPay stays off until the maintainer says so (see rule-2); AutoPay-on-web not pursued. Q8: value updates are entered monthly as the amount increased since investment; keep EACH update as a record and notify the client every time their investment is updated. ROI form (simple vs annualised) not answered; default simple return %.
entries.retiredWhy: Question answers are decisions, not rules (maintainer 2026-11-14). Recorded as decisions DEC-4 to DEC-8, group admin-improvements.

entries.title: Decision 2026-11-13: plans/admin-improvements.md approved; Phase A starts on parallel tracks
entries.text: Maintainer replied 'Yes I do' to: approve the plan, commit it, and start Phase A on tally tracks with their own worktrees. Covers opening tracks/worktrees, npm ci of locked dependencies inside them for one-shot checks, committing on track branches and landing through the tally queue onto local main (not pushing). Not covered: container runtime for the testcontainers integration suite (gate G2), deploys, APK exports, real customer mail, enabling payments, Phase D destructive step, identity rule changes pending Q-017/Q-024/Q-025. Lane rules: adminQueries.ts must not grow (move touched hooks into feature query modules); admin-money.ts untouched in Phase A; new contract files per lane in Phase B; migrations 061/062/063 reserved for C1/C2/C3.

entries.title: Decisions 2026-11-13 (second round): containers, SIP, maturity, identity, data reform, reviews, ROI
entries.text: Maintainer answers via in-chat questions, 2026-11-13. G2: container runtime allowed for the testcontainers integration suite (throwaway PostgreSQL, cleaned up). Q-021: admin-tracked SIP schedule (monthly amount, fund, start month, months; monthly recordings linked to a month; client sees N of M paid; no collection); maturity date per client fund holding. Q-024: BOTH an audited admin contact-correction action for clients who have not set a password (old links retired, new invite to corrected address) AND closed accounts releasing their email/phone. Q-017: admin invite (set) links valid 24 hours; email codes and reset links stay 10 minutes. Q-025: setting the password through the invite link marks that email verified. Q-019: reform fixes duplicates and fills missing new details (categories, maturity dates, SIP schedules, nominees); dev copy has names/emails/phones masked. Duplicates: duplicate investments get reversal entries keeping both rows; duplicate client accounts are closed and merged into the real one only after the maintainer confirms each pair. Q-020: client reviews wanted, admins only, with client profile; nothing public. Q-022: dashboards show simple return % as main figure plus annualised (XIRR) secondary. Q-023: app-update mail keeps going to all active clients.

entries.title: Decisions 2026-11-13 (revised): invites, verification, reform scope, bank-transfer investing, reviews later
entries.text: Supersedes rule-8 where they differ. In force: containers allowed for the integration suite; admin-tracked SIP schedule (amount, fund, start month, months; monthly recordings linked; client sees N of M paid; no collection); maturity date per client fund holding; admin contact correction before password set + closed accounts release email/phone (history kept); dashboards show simple % plus XIRR; app-update mail to all. REVISED: Q-017 invite links stay short (10 min); instead the admin must be able to regenerate a new invite link easily, incl. after expiry or cancellation. Q-025 setting a password does NOT verify the email; the email code step stays. Q-019 no standalone cleanup project: reform/clean the DB only when something requires it, client data only, no data lost, rehearsed on dev with masked copy. Clients pay SIPs and investments directly to the company bank account; the admin records them and clients must see invested amounts reflected seamlessly in their dashboard whether the gateway is on or off. Q-020 reviews wanted but deferred; fix bugs first. Maintainer delegates: work out what else such apps need and simplify complex flows so client and admin have a seamless experience.

entries.title: Decision 2026-11-13 (G12): expire stale pending online payments whose pay-by time has passed
entries.text: Maintainer chose: mark old pending online payments/orders created before payments were turned off as expired. Scope: only attempts/payments whose checkout expiry (plus the configured grace) has passed; one-time or reconciliation-pass step that uses the existing expiry path (paymentsRepository markPaymentExpired and the canonical outcome flow), audited, idempotent, never deletes or rewrites rows, never moves money, and never touches a payment the provider might still settle once payments return (if the gateway is later configured, normal reconciliation applies). Clients stop seeing 'awaiting payment'. This retires in-flight state deliberately under RULES rule 11 with the impact stated: those clients would have to start a new payment once payments return. Needs an integration test proving only expired-by-time rows change.
entries.retiredWhy: A decision, not a rule (DEC-28). Recorded as decision DEC-24.

entries.title: Decision 2026-11-13: no bank details or payment instructions; monthly investments notify 'Investment added'
entries.text:
Maintainer, in chat during Phase B: "I wouldn't be adding/recording any bank details or payment methods included, only a category that adding monthly investments which for the clients will be receiving notifications as investment added." Effects:
- G11 no longer includes a How-to-invest FAQ. The maintainer's only remaining G11 step is publishing featureFlags.onlinePayments=false after B8 lands.
- B8 drops the How-to-invest card and any copy telling clients how or where to pay. Pay/invest buttons are still hidden when the flag is false, with at most one neutral line ("recorded by the BeOnEdge team").
- B1: monthly investment (and earlier investment) recordings notify the client with the title "Investment added". Correction keeps neutral wording.
- Agents never put bank details or payment methods in code, copy, FAQ seeds or emails.

entries.title: Decision 2026-11-13: recorded investments also email the client the amount with 'check your app'
entries.text:
Maintainer, in chat: "Also an email notification of the amount recorded for that client notifying about the investment added to their app, and to check their app." Effects:
- When the admin records a monthly or earlier investment, the client gets an email titled "Investment added", in addition to the in-app notification. It gives the amount (from paise), fund and date, asks them to open the app, and includes the CLIENT_WEB_APP_URL line when configured.
- Corrections send no email.
- Delivery: one email per recording, queued in the recording transaction, idempotent on replay. Amount and names go in the sealed payload. A per-template send guard cancels after reversal, closure or tombstone, bound to the email revision at queue time.
- Needs migration 062, which only widens the email_deliveries.template_check list. AdminEmailTemplateKey is a request filter, so the delivery response stays z.string() and released admin APKs are safe.
- Built by lane b-receipts. No bank details or payment instructions (rule-11).

entries.title: Decisions 2026-11-14: payments halted, no reference number, recordings confirmed, maturity choices for client
entries.text:
Maintainer, in chat, answering question rows 16-18:
- Payments: "i don't want to add or change anything about it, only asked you to fix some bugs and disable it." AutoPay and everything payment-gateway related is halted until the maintainer says to resume. E2 stays as built and dormant; no further payment work. Row 17 (missed AutoPay months) is answered by this: no change.
- Row 16: no reference number (UTR or any other) on admin recordings. Task E4-bank-reference is dropped.
- Recordings confirmed as built (B1/B2/B5): the Record action on the admin user page offers a Monthly investment category; every recording is kept with its date as a ledger/log the admin keeps, reflected in the client's app. Gap: the admin ledger tab shows the effective date only, not when the row was recorded.
- Row 18 maturity: options are (1) withdraw the invested amount with returns; (2) reinvest the previous amount as a one-time investment, then start recording the next SIP; (3) increase the SIP's time period (replaces "reinvest as a new SIP"). Options never pop up for the client by themselves. The admin is notified first (30-day launch prompt, confirmed), then either resolves directly after talking to the client, or sends the options to that client, who gets an email and an in-app notification and can choose in the app. Both client and admin can decide.

entries.title: When two sources disagree, the higher one wins
entries.text: Highest first: these rules; the decisions; the code as last verified, with the checks record and the build log; the commit bodies, which say why; the open questions and what each says to do meanwhile; the plans, which say what is intended, not built. A plan that differs from the code is corrected, unless the code breaks a rule or a decision; then the code is fixed.
entries.tailor: Is there a source outside this repository (a specification, another system's documents) that wins over this repository's summary of it? Name it and where it is.
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md 'Authority' sets the order of sources here; RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: Never push, release or deploy unasked
entries.text: Pushing, publishing, releasing and deploying are the operator's to do or to ask for. An agent builds and verifies on this machine, and never runs a command with raised privileges.
entries.tailor: How is this project released and deployed, and who runs it? Name the commands an agent never runs.
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md rules 2 and 14, and rule-16; RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: Credentials belong to the operator
entries.text: Never print a secret's value, never commit one, and never create, change or remove a credential or a .env file. Code reads a secret from its environment and, when it is missing, names it and stops.
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md rule 3; RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: Change nothing outside this repository that cannot be undone
entries.text: Until the operator names what this project must never do, these are forbidden: spending money, sending a message to a person, and any request that changes another system.
entries.tailor: What must this project never do, whatever the tests say (place an order, charge a card, send mail, write to a system it does not own)? Each is a rule of its own.
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md rules 1 to 3, rule-16 and rule-17; RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: What this project does not own is read-only
entries.text: Data, services, containers and files that belong to something else on this machine are never written, moved, restarted, pruned or deleted. Every command is scoped to this project's own names, never to everything on the machine.
entries.tailor: What shares this project's machine or feeds it data? Name what is read-only, and the names (project, containers, folders) that mark what is this project's own.
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md rule 3 (never stop an unfamiliar service; local one-shot checks only); RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: A result that breaks an invariant is wrong, whatever the tests say
entries.text: Until the operator names this project's invariants, a change that alters what a result means is the operator's to decide, never the builder's.
entries.tailor: What must always hold in this project's results (no look-ahead, no money created or lost, nothing sent twice)? Each is a rule of its own, with the test that enforces it.
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md rules 4, 5, 6 and 11 name this project's invariants; RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: Unknown stays unknown
entries.text: A value that is missing, unreadable or inconsistent is reported as missing and refused. It is never filled in, guessed or repaired silently, and every value shown traces back to where it came from.
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md rule 4; RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: Do not invent a value a result depends on
entries.text: A price, a rate, a limit or a size that is not configured or verified gets no default. Show it as unconfigured and refuse the run that needs it, naming it. A number that must exist and is not verified is labelled unverified wherever it is printed.
entries.tailor: Which values must never be defaulted here?
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md rule 7; RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: Stored formats stay readable by the previous release
entries.text: A rollback swaps the code and keeps the data. So a schema, a file format or a stored record changes additively: add a field in one release, and drop one only in a later release.
entries.tailor: What does this project store for good, and which formats does this rule cover?
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md rule 11; RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: Open decisions and gates are the operator's, and only those
entries.text: A choice is the operator's when it changes what a result means or costs, what is stored for good, what the project may do, or an existing decision. It becomes a question that states the conservative behaviour to build meanwhile, and is never decided in code. Every other choice is the builder's: make it, record it in one line, and go on. Report a gate's evidence; never declare it closed.
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md 'Authority' and rule 16; RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: Write the test first and see it fail on its assertion
entries.text: A failure to compile proves nothing. A test added for code that already exists is proven once, by breaking that code by hand and seeing the assertion fail. A fixture written from the code's own belief proves nothing. Never weaken a failing test: decide which side is wrong and say so in the commit.
entries.tailor: Where do the tests live, what coverage must hold, and which areas are tested whatever the coverage says?
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md rule 10 governs tests here: tests only where silent failure is expensive, each new guard proven by a controlled negative case; write-tests-first conflicts with it; RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: No comments in source
entries.text: Name things so the code reads on its own, and put the why in the commit body. A script that guards a dangerous step is the exception: its gates carry their reasons.
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md rule 9; RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: Keep it simple
entries.text: No hardening against a threat that does not apply. No abstraction, switch or option until something concrete needs it.
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md rule 11, last bullet; RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: Source and test files stay under 400 lines, 800 at most
entries.text: A change that takes a file past 400 lines splits it in the same change. Lockfiles, generated files, fixtures, data and reports are exempt.
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md rule 12; RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: No silenced warnings, and nothing without a reader
entries.text: The linter and the type checker run with warnings as errors, and the source silences none. A new field or option gets its reader in the same change; when the reader comes later, so does the field.
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md rule 13; RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: One commit per task, and main stays linear
entries.text: Each commit builds and passes the tests on its own. Sessions working at the same time each commit to their own track's branch in its own worktree, rebase it on main after every task and land it by fast-forward through tally. Main never holds a merge commit, and a track's branch is never pushed.
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md rule 14 and WORKFLOW.md; tally landing keeps main linear; RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: The commit body is the log
entries.text: The subject is type(scope): an imperative summary, under about 70 characters. The body says why, the tradeoffs, the earlier belief it corrects and the numbers it relies on, and never restates the diff. One identity, the repository's, and no line that names an agent or a tool.
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md rule 14; RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: When you fix a bug, ask whether it is an instance or a class
entries.text: Search the code around it for the same shape, fix what you find, and say in the commit what you searched.
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md rule 15; RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: Collect questions; do not stop to ask them
entries.text: Add a question only for a choice that is the operator's. Take the conservative reading (the one that refuses, holds or reports unknown, never one that invents a value), write it as the question's meanwhile, build it, and keep going. Stop only for what only the operator can do: a credential, a push, a deploy, raised privileges.
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md rule 16, which also forbids the shortcut for fund movement, identity, destructive changes, real sends and deployment; RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: Report real numbers, measured once
entries.text: A count, a timing or a size is measured, not remembered, by whoever claims it, and written down with its command. A speed claim also names the machine and the data. Anyone else measures it again only when it looks wrong or a decision rests on it, never when its code has not changed.
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md rule 17; RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: Trust the code over the docs
entries.text: Check a document's claim against the source before building on it. When they differ, settle it by the order of authority and correct the one that lost, once.
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md 'Authority' and 'Preparing context' step 7; RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: The records describe the code by the end of each milestone
entries.text: A milestone is not done until the ledger, the checks record, the build log and the context entries its changes touch say what was built. Never leave a record that describes behaviour the code no longer has.
entries.retiredWhy: Covered by RULES.md rule 18 and 'Updating documents and plans'; RULES.md is the one rulebook (DEC-35).

entries.title: Scratch stays under .temp/
entries.text: Everything an agent writes that is not part of the repository (plans, notes, logs, throwaway scripts and builds) goes under .temp/ in the checkout it works in, one folder per track. Nothing there is ever cited: what a record relies on is recorded through tally.

entries.title: Decide once
entries.text: A choice recorded as a decision, in the build log, or settled by the order of authority is not reopened on opinion by a later step or agent. Evidence reopens it: a failing test or a measurement that shows a builder's choice wrong corrects it, and that is recorded; one that shows a decision wrong becomes a question.
entries.retiredWhy: replaced by rule-49

entries.title: Record once
entries.text: Each fact has one home: a decision in the decisions, an open question in the questions, what was built and measured in the build log, the code as last verified in the checks record, progress in the ledger, and why in the commit body. Everything else points to that home and never copies it.
entries.retiredWhy: replaced by rule-50

entries.title: Read once
entries.text: Read what the brief and the task name, not every document. Hand a helper these rules and the paths and ids it needs, never "read everything".
entries.retiredWhy: replaced by rule-51

entries.title: Check once
entries.text: Before running a check, compare the code fingerprint with the checks record: while they match, the record is the verification, and nothing runs again. While working, run the checks of the part you changed, and the tests before each commit. The whole sweep runs once, before the milestone's last commit and before review.
entries.tailor: What is this project's whole sweep, command by command?
entries.retiredWhy: replaced by rule-52

entries.title: Review once, against the plan
entries.text: A review checks, in this order: that every item the milestone was to deliver exists, by path and test name; the rules that tests cannot see, read against the diff; the sweep, once at HEAD; and the numbers a decision rests on. It blocks only on a missing item, a failing check, a broken rule, behaviour that differs from a decision or a plan, or a wrong number. A follow-up looks only at the fix commits.

entries.title: Three attempts, then move on
entries.text: When the same failure survives three different attempts, stop that path. Record what was tried and the error, add a question if only the operator can unblock it, and go on with the next task that does not depend on it. The stopped task stays open, and the milestone's report names it.

Run logs go under <repo>/.temp/tally/logs/<track>/ so they outlive the worktree. Nothing there is ever cited: what a record relies on is recorded through tally or the plan.

entries.title: Check once
entries.text: While working, run the checks of the part you changed in the pinned Node 22 container (tools/node22-container/run.sh; howto-2), and the unit's npm run check before each commit. The whole sweep runs once, on a clean checkout, before a phase's close and before its final review: packages/contracts npm run check and npm run build; backend_controller npm run check; backend_controller npm run test:integration -- --coverage.enabled=false; frontend_stack_ts npm run check, npm run build:client and npm run build:admin. A landing's per-commit checks do not replace it. Record the sweep as tally evidence with its counts, and do not rerun it while the code is unchanged.

entries.title: Review once, against the plan
entries.text: Every lane gets one independent review before it lands, against the plan and the decisions: every item it was to deliver exists, by path and test name; the rules tests cannot see (RULES.md rules 4, 9, 10, 11, 13), read against the diff; and the numbers a decision rests on. It blocks only on a missing item, a broken rule, behaviour that differs from a decision, or a wrong number. A follow-up looks only at the fix commits. A destructive or irreversible change (RULES.md rule 11) also gets a database review.

entries.title: Three attempts, then move on
entries.text: When the same failure survives three different attempts, stop that path. Record what was tried and the error, add a question if only the operator can unblock it, and go on with the next task that does not depend on it. The stopped task stays open, and the milestone's report names it.
